bio:
Born in Edmonton and raised in Consort, Alberta, k.d. lang emerged in the 1980s with a knowingly theatrical take on country music that drew from Patsy Cline, western swing and the energy of punk-era alternative culture. With the Reclines, she built a reputation as both a powerful vocalist and an artist willing to stretch country conventions, then moved into broader recognition with Shadowland and the GRAMMY-winning Absolute Torch and Twang.

Her 1992 album Ingenue marked a decisive shift toward sophisticated adult pop and torch-song writing. Its signature single, “Constant Craving,” won the GRAMMY for Best Female Pop Vocal Performance and became the recording most closely associated with lang’s ability to make restraint feel dramatic. She continued moving between original songwriting, standards and interpretation, including the Canadian-songbook project Hymns of the 49th Parallel and the Tony Bennett collaboration A Wonderful World.

Lang’s significance is musical and cultural. Her fluid movement between country, pop, folk and standards helped resist narrow genre expectations, while her visibility as an openly lesbian major recording artist made her an important figure in queer representation. A Canadian Music Hall of Fame inductee with four GRAMMY Awards and multiple JUNO Awards, she remains one of Canada’s most distinctive vocal stylists.

Kai Banks is a rapper and recording artist in London, Ontario's 4DaTribe collective, part of a new generation of Canadian hip-hop artists emerging from the city. His solo catalogue includes The Kaible and 08 JETTA, while Too Deep For The Outro with La Reezy and Mileena is his Northern Dial library credit.

Toronto native Kalisway is an alternative R&B and funk artist, songwriter and producer whose bright, groove-heavy music draws on soul, funk and hip-hop. Her catalogue includes HIT 'EM WITH THE FUNK and the album A Kid From Toronto.
Hudson Bay, Saskatchewan singer-songwriter Kalsey Kulyk is a Canadian country artist whose contemporary recordings draw on traditional country storytelling and prairie roots.

Toronto-born, Vancouver-raised hip-hop artist Kapok is a Mayan-Canadian rapper, songwriter and producer whose work blends rap with soul, jazz and R&B. Raised in Vancouver's Strathcona neighbourhood, he has collaborated with artists including De La Soul, Moka Only, T3 and Potatohead People while building an independent West Coast catalogue.
Dakar-born, Québec-raised singer-songwriter Karim Ouellet was a Senegalese-Canadian artist whose French-language pop blended soul, reggae, rock and electronic influences.

Scarborough MC Karisma is a member of Monolith, the long-running Canadian hip-hop collective formed from Toronto crews Lyrical Coalition and The Horde. His recorded appearances include Monolith material and the Mastermind posse cut Let’s Make A Record Deal Episode 2 alongside Dan-e-o, Korry Deez, Grimace Love and Black Cat.
Lebanese-born Canadian singer, songwriter and producer Karl Wolf built a Toronto-based pop and R&B career known for polished crossover production and international radio singles.

Karma Sutra is an Ottawa-rooted, Toronto-based rapper whose music combines melodic hip-hop with introspective and emotionally direct writing. His catalogue includes the project Sad Shorty and other independent releases tied to Ontario's contemporary rap scene. Northern Dial carries Karma Sutra as part of its Canadian hip-hop catalogue.

Kash Phat is a Canada-based Ghanaian singer and electronic artist associated with Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario. His catalogue spans hip-hop, R&B and Afropop-influenced releases including Project 1: Kash to the World and To Her, and the Sault Ste. Marie Music Project lists Kash-phat among artists from the city.
Saskatoon singer-songwriter Katie Tupper is a Canadian soul and R&B artist known for warm vocals, understated grooves and intimate contemporary songwriting.

Windsor, Ontario singer-songwriter Kelsi Mayne built her career independently, bringing country songwriting into contact with the R&B, soul and pop sounds that travelled across the Detroit River into her hometown. She first developed as a live performer while studying nursing, singing regularly at a Windsor country bar before moving into festival stages, radio and a self-managed recording career. Her 2020 debut album As I Go established that mix of country structure, forceful vocals and wider pop-soul influence.

Mayne’s catalogue continued to grow through singles including "All or Nothing," "Breaking Bad" and "For The Record." "Breaking Bad" reached the Top 50 at Canadian country radio, while "For The Record" earned placement through SiriusXM’s The Highway and major Canadian country playlists. She has also appeared at major Canadian country festivals including Boots and Hearts, Big Valley Jamboree and the Calgary Stampede, while earning multiple CMAOntario nominations and recognition through the International Songwriting Competition.

Her 2026 sophomore album Out of the Blue pushed the independent career into a new phase after years of writing in Nashville and steadily widening her audience. Mayne matters in the Canadian country landscape because her work is rooted in a border-city musical environment where country, Motown, rock and R&B overlap, giving her a sound that is recognizably country without being stylistically narrow.

Toronto native Kennedy Rd. is an R&B singer-songwriter whose atmospheric, emotionally direct sound draws on 1990s and early-2000s R&B influences. Her catalogue includes the Feelings Cafe EP and collaborations across Toronto's contemporary R&B scene.

Toronto singer-songwriter Khadijah Lopez brings classic soul and contemporary R&B together through warm vocals and emotionally direct writing. A Remix Project alum, she has participated in songwriting camps and mentorship programs, contributed songs to television and continued building her independent catalogue through releases and collaborations including Over, Again with pHoenix Pagliacci.

Kheir is a Montréal producer and beatmaker active in Quebec's francophone hip-hop scene. His production credits include QCLTUR releases and work with artists including KNLO, while his 2025 collaborative album blues beldi with Nawfal paired rap, Maghrebi influence and jazz-informed production. Their track archive 2001 is his Northern Dial library credit.

Kid Sharif is a Victoria-born, Vancouver-based hip-hop artist who began releasing music independently in 2018. His early work documented Vancouver nightlife and helped establish him within the city's emerging rap scene. Northern Dial carries Kid Sharif as part of its contemporary West Coast Canadian hip-hop catalogue.
Toronto-born Kim Davis is a Canadian R&B and soul singer-songwriter whose solo work blends R&B, hip-hop, soul and reggae and has earned Juno nominations in both reggae and R&B categories.

Canadian Eurodance singer and producer Kim Esty built a run of dance releases in the 1990s before reaching a wider audience as the featured vocalist on The Boomtang Boys’ hit singles Squeeze Toy and Pictures. Squeeze Toy topped the Canadian singles chart and won Best Dance Video at the 1999 MuchMusic Video Awards.
St. John's-born singer-songwriter Kim Stockwood is a Canadian pop and roots artist whose career includes solo hits, songwriting, radio work and membership in the trio Shaye.
Vancouver-based Filipino-Canadian musician and visual artist Kimmortal blends hip-hop, R&B, soul and experimental music with queer and diasporic storytelling.

King Bliss is a Toronto emcee rooted in the city's underground hip-hop and cypher scene. His catalogue includes tracks such as Top Shotta, Pocket Dial and Writing the Wrongs, with a style built around lyricism and social commentary. Northern Dial carries King Bliss as part of Toronto's independent rap community.

King Dapz is a Scarborough rapper associated with Toronto's independent hip-hop scene. He has released solo material and collaborated with fellow Scarborough artist Gangis Khan, with tracks including Drip, Done and Angels (Freestyle). Northern Dial carries King Dapz as part of its contemporary Toronto rap catalogue.

Toronto-born MC King Reign was a respected Canadian hip-hop storyteller known for detailed, soulful writing, collaborations with artists including Saukrates and Kardinal Offishall and a lasting influence on the city's rap community.
Toronto-based band Kiwi Jr. is a Canadian indie-rock group known for jangly guitars, literate lyrics and sharp power-pop songwriting.

kkanji is the stage name of Kaelan Hachey, a Montreal-based pop and R&B artist whose catalogue blends indie pop, contemporary R&B and alternative songwriting. His releases include You've Still Got Time, Six String Chemistry and Rowdy, alongside collaborations with other Montreal artists including Luka Ferraro. Northern Dial carries kkanji as part of its contemporary Montreal independent music catalogue.

Montréal artist, producer and songwriter Koko Love developed his approach through years of performing in public spaces, including busking in the city's metro system, before recording under the name Miko and eventually relaunching under the Koko Love identity. That background helps explain the directness of his music: rather than separating production craft from performance, he built a sound around live musicianship, alternative pop, soul and indie rock while remaining closely involved in writing and production.

The 2025 debut album The Cost of Freedom became the clearest statement of that approach. Written, produced and recorded with Soran, the project brought in collaborators including Zach Zoya and Yuki Dreams Again and was mixed in Montréal before being mastered by Randy Merrill at Sterling Sound. "Man I'm Not," featuring Zach Zoya, became a notable Canadian radio moment, reaching No. 3 on CBC Radio and later appearing on CBC's list of the 100 best songs of 2025. Around the same period, Koko Love toured North America with Kyle Dion and contributed production work to Dion's music.

Koko Love is still an emerging artist, but his career already reflects a useful Montréal story: a musician moving from street-level performance and an earlier artistic identity into a self-produced project with national radio traction and increasingly international collaborators. His significance lies less in awards or legacy milestones than in the way his work connects Montréal's alternative, R&B and producer communities through a hands-on, independent recording practice.

KOLA is a Montreal producer and recording artist whose music is rooted in hip-hop and beat-driven production. Raised in Montreal, he has developed an independent catalogue that reflects the city's multilingual and stylistically diverse music culture. Northern Dial carries KOLA as part of its Montreal producer and hip-hop catalogue.
Scarborough rapper Korry Deez, whose name also appears in the library as Korey Deez, is a Canadian hip-hop artist best known as a member of IRS and the Monolith collective.
Scarborough rapper Korry Deez is a Canadian hip-hop artist best known as a member of IRS and the Monolith collective, part of Toronto's influential late-1990s and early-2000s underground rap scene.

KOTO? is a London, Ontario-rooted rapper and producer active in Toronto and a member of the 4DaTribe collective. His music draws heavily on boom-bap and lo-fi hip-hop, pairing compact, sample-driven production with dense lyricism across projects including Mornington Me and 4DaTribe Disc Two. DerekFisher, with Soft Eyez and Chai Sully, is his Northern Dial library credit.

Montréal rapper Kris the $pirit first built a following as half of The Posterz before launching a solo run rooted in the city's underground hip-hop scene and his own production-heavy, introspective style.
Ottawa-born singer-songwriter Kristina Maria is a Canadian pop and R&B artist whose early-2010s catalogue combined dance-pop production with melodic radio songwriting.

Kubla is a Canadian soul and R&B singer-songwriter, producer, guitarist and bandleader based in Toronto. Raised on Canada's West Coast by musician parents, he built his independent career after moving to Toronto, blending jazz-informed musicianship with soul, R&B and pop across releases including Close to the Sun, Sounds from Deep Down and Bodies Dancing.

Kwncy is a Toronto-born and raised singer-songwriter whose music blends alternative R&B, neo-soul and lo-fi pop. Her catalogue includes CROOKED, DOWNTOWN, Territorial and the 2026 project St Lucie Drive, alongside collaborations with Canadian artists including DijahSB and RUSSELL!.

Kxng Wooz is a Halifax-based Canadian hip-hop artist whose music pairs introspective lyricism with contemporary rap production. A longtime part of Nova Scotia's independent scene, he has released projects including Entering The..., Redemption and MALIK and collaborated with artists such as Ghettosocks, Aquakultre, Timbuktu and Leila Dey.

La Dynastie des Morniers is a Montréal hip-hop collective closely connected to Muzion and the city's Saint-Michel rap community. Emerging from the same mid-1990s network that produced Wolfpack, Akadémia and Muzion, the collective included Montréal rappers such as Le Voyou and appeared on Muzion's 2002 album J'Rêvolutionne.

LA Luv is a Toronto hip-hop DJ and artist associated with Michie Mee and the early Canadian rap scene. He later became part of the Dream Warriors orbit and appears throughout documented histories of Toronto hip-hop's formative years. Northern Dial carries LA Luv as part of its foundational Canadian hip-hop catalogue.
Montréal art-punk collective La Sécurité makes wiry Canadian post-punk built around jumpy rhythms, minimal hooks and playful, danceable arrangements.

Lais is a Toronto-based R&B singer and rapper whose moody independent catalogue drew early attention from OVO Sound Radio. Releases including SESSION ONE, Give Me One More and the 2018 single Once account for his four Northern Dial library credits.

Lan'do is a Canadian-born rapper and songwriter who was raised in Jamaica before returning to a Toronto-rooted music community. His genre-blurring solo work draws on hip-hop, dancehall and international influences, and he has also collaborated with Toronto collective No Tourists. His appearance on X10Land's 2023 single Walking With Wolves with Junia-T, Private Name Private Number, Victory and Patrik Kabongo is his Northern Dial library credit.

Lane Hall is a Halifax, Nova Scotia soul collective led vocally by JRDN with musical direction from Richard 'Nulo' McNeil. The project brings together musicians from the Halifax scene around live soul, R&B and groove-oriented arrangements. Northern Dial carries Lane Hall as part of its Atlantic Canadian soul and R&B catalogue.

Latoya is a Canadian R&B vocalist associated with producer Dub J's Kitchener-Waterloo and Toronto-area hip-hop network. Dub J identifies Latoya among the Canadian talent he produced during the growth of his Q It Up Records catalogue. Northern Dial carries Latoya as part of the Canadian R&B and hip-hop ecosystem surrounding that era.

British-born, British Columbia-raised Lauren Spencer Smith is a Canadian pop singer-songwriter whose confessional ballads and powerhouse vocals broke internationally with Fingers Crossed and led to multiple Juno nominations.

Lazyeye is a Toronto producer closely associated with Mississauga rapper AR Paisley and Canada's Punjabi hip-hop scene. He produced much of Paisley's debut album Timeless and has continued collaborating on releases including G-Shock, Legends Never Die and Moose World. Northern Dial carries Lazyeye as part of its contemporary Canadian hip-hop producer catalogue.

Jamaican-born, Toronto-raised Canadian R&B singer-songwriter Leila Dey blends soulful vocals with hip-hop, reggae and jazz influences. A longtime fixture in Toronto’s R&B scene, she has released projects including DETOUR, opened for artists such as Jessie Reyez and built a catalogue rooted in vulnerable, cinematic songwriting.

Leith is the pop project of Toronto-born singer-songwriter Jessie Munro. Her atmospheric pop balances bright hooks with introspective songwriting, with releases including Birthdays in July, Running Wild and the 2026 EP Sad In The Sun. Northern Dial carries Leith as part of its contemporary Canadian pop catalogue.

Toronto multi-instrumentalist, songwriter and producer Leland Whitty is best known as BADBADNOTGOOD's saxophonist and a versatile collaborator whose work crosses jazz, hip-hop, soul, scoring and production.

LeMind is an Ottawa rapper, producer and audio engineer working in francophone hip-hop. Originally from Ottawa, he has built a catalogue shaped by introspective writing and self-produced rap. Northern Dial carries LeMind as part of its Ontario francophone hip-hop catalogue.

Oshawa-born Lennon Stella first reached a wide audience alongside her younger sister Maisy. Their stripped-down cover performances circulated widely online before both sisters joined the television drama Nashville, where Lennon spent six seasons playing Maddie Conrad. That unusual apprenticeship put her in front of a mass audience while she was still developing as a musician, singer and songwriter rather than arriving as a conventional label-built pop act.

Stella began separating her own musical identity from the show with the 2018 EP Love, Me. The project shifted toward atmospheric contemporary pop, and collaborations including Jonas Blue and Liam Payne's "Polaroid" and The Chainsmokers and Illenium's "Takeaway" expanded her international audience. Her 2020 debut album Three. Two. One. followed with songs including "Kissing Other People," "Older Than I Am" and "Fear of Being Alone," presenting a more self-contained version of the intimate, restrained pop sound she had been building.

Stella's significance lies partly in the transition itself. She moved from a Canadian family act and television role into a credible adult recording career without simply reproducing the country-pop world that introduced her. Three. Two. One. reached the Canadian albums Top 10, and its mixture of diaristic writing, electronic detail and soft-focus R&B textures placed Stella within the generation of Canadian pop artists whose careers developed simultaneously through television, streaming and global collaborations.
Toronto-born rapper Lex Leosis is a Canadian hip-hop artist known for dynamic flows, storytelling and her earlier work in the all-women rap collective The Sorority.
